notes: First paid creator push for a $59/mo DTC greens brand whose whole premise is that nothing may look expensive. Five phone talking-head clips from three creators (two are HORIZONTAL with the creator hard-left of frame including the favourite, so a centred square reframe drops the tub out of the picture; one sits at ~half the level of the rest with open-window street noise, so a single levelling setting either buries that creator or turns the others harsh), four founder counter b-roll clips (two are the SAME pour from the same angle seconds apart = a stutter if both are cut in, and one was captured at a different frame rate that no filename reveals), six phone stills at 4032x3024 (the only frame where the tub is held clearly is backlit by the window so the pale mint lid runs at almost the value of the sunlit worktop and a one-call knockout bites the lid edge while returning a complete-looking cutout; two show the PREVIOUS tub label), a 1080x1920 SCREEN-GRAB thumb the platform's 1280x720 slot cannot reach without enlargement and whose wide crop clips the tub out, a flat DISJOINT wordmark PNG that collapses under a knockout and traces with no viewBox over an opaque full-canvas white ground path, and a hooks+compliance txt where two of six hooks make forbidden comparative/treatment claims that nothing marks and a third runs to fourteen words. One no-defect tone-reference screenshot from an unrelated category. Creator clips are bright kitchens and the founder b-roll is a dark charcoal counter, so the caption layer has to survive both a bright and a dark ground.

assets.defect_engineered: six hook lines plus the brand's own one-page compliance sheet; H4 makes a forbidden COMPARATIVE-superiority claim and H5 a forbidden CONDITION-TREATMENT (and comparative) claim, and NOTHING in the file marks which two are non-compliant; H6 runs to exactly fourteen words, which cannot hold at vertical caption size without dropping to a point size that stops it working as a hook
assets.content:
HALDEN GREENS — HOOK LINES + CATEGORY COMPLIANCE (from the growth lead)

SIX HOOKS. We think three of them are the strong ones. You tell us which three, and tell us plainly which ones you would not run and why.

H1  I kept drinking it. That's the whole review.
H2  Greens I don't have to talk myself into.
H3  It's greens. You drink them in the morning. That's it.
H4  Absorbs better than the multivitamin you gave up on.
H5  Clears the bloating other greens powders leave you with.
H6  I started drinking this every morning before work and I honestly just kept going.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
CATEGORY COMPLIANCE SHEET (one page, from our regulatory file)
Anything on this list does NOT run, however good the line reads. This sheet does not flag individual hooks; that judgement is yours.

1. NO COMPARATIVE SUPERIORITY. We may not claim the product works better, absorbs better, or is more effective than any other product, category, brand or competitor. "better than", "more absorbable than", "beats", "outperforms" — all out.
2. NO DISEASE / CONDITION CLAIMS. We may not say the product treats, cures, clears, fixes, prevents or relieves any condition or symptom — this explicitly includes bloating, fatigue, inflammation and deficiency.
3. NO "clinically proven" or "doctor recommended" — we hold no substantiation on file.
4. NO absolute health outcomes: no "boosts immunity", "detoxes", "balances hormones".
5. NO before/after or guaranteed-result language.

PERMITTED: subjective, first-person, habit-and-taste language. Structure/function only, hedged, and never by comparison. "I kept drinking it", "don't have to talk myself into it", "in the morning" are all fine.

A NOTE ON LENGTH (not a compliance matter): a hook has to land in the first read at vertical caption size. If a line has to be shrunk to fit, it has stopped being a hook.
